stories.title: Canada plans retaliatory tariffs after U.S. trade talks collapse
stories.summary: Canada says it will answer new 50% U.S. tariffs with dollar-for-dollar measures beginning September 8. The dispute covers goods including steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, paper and electronics, making the breakdown especially consequential for Michigan's cross-border manufacturing and agricultural economy.

stories.title: Judge dismisses federal challenge to Washtenaw County immigration policies
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled that Washtenaw County's sheriff, prosecutor and commissioners did not violate federal law by declining to assist with federal immigration enforcement. The ruling says the federal government cannot compel the county to use local jail space and resources for federal priorities.

stories.title: Michigan Republicans finalize 2026 statewide ticket
stories.summary: Republican delegates formally nominated state Rep. Jay DeBoyer as John James' running mate at the party convention in Mount Pleasant. The gathering emphasized state issues and party unity while rarely mentioning President Trump, whose approval ratings have weakened ahead of the general election.

stories.title: Michigan revenue runs modestly ahead of forecasts
stories.summary: Michigan collected about $3.1 billion in July, nearly 7% more than a year earlier. The general fund is roughly $455 million to $459 million above year-to-date projections, while the School Aid Fund is about $195 million to $220 million ahead, offering limited breathing room before expected difficult budget years.

stories.title: Detroit property-tax relief program returns
stories.summary: Wayne County's Pay as You Stay program is again available to qualifying Detroit homeowners, removing penalties, interest and fees from delinquent property taxes. Residents must first qualify for the income-based HOPE exemption; the 2026 enrollment deadline is November 6.

stories.title: Lathrup Village begins building its first city arboretum
stories.summary: Lathrup Village is turning public green space into an educational tree garden centered on Michigan-native species. The project is part of the city's broader green-infrastructure work to manage stormwater, reduce erosion and strengthen the community's mature tree canopy.

stories.title: Michigan-led effort revives an endangered butterfly population
stories.summary: Researchers and conservation partners have expanded the known U.S. population of the Poweshiek skipperling from nine wild butterflies in 2022 to roughly 1,300 in captive and restored populations. The effort combines breeding at John Ball Zoo with releases into restored habitat, including sites in Southeast Michigan.
